ES 350 aggregate figures:
- 2012 ES 350 average list price in Milwaukee: $14,354 at an average of 117,135 miles.
- 2012 ES 350 nationwide average: $13,317, from $6,999.
- 2011 ES 350 Milwaukee average trade-in value: about $4,488 at an average of 136,469 miles. This suggests dealer retail of $8-11k for about 130k-mile 2010-2012 cars (estimate).
- 2009 ES 350 nationwide average: $9,297, from $5,107.
- KBB Madison ES 350 listings run $15,000-$41,998 (6 cars, none under budget). KBB Milwaukee runs $8,995-$48,569.
- iSeeCars Milwaukee 2014-2018 ES 350s: $16,900-$27,676.
So a 2012-2015 ES 350 under $13.5k usually means more than 120k miles, or an independent lot.

IS 250 (AWD common):
- 2006-2007 AWD: $6,000-$7,995. Examples: Golden Cars 2007 AWD at $6,900; a 2007 AWD with 150,984 miles at $7,995; a Facebook Marketplace 2006 with 270k miles at $6,000-6,500.
- A private Milwaukee IS 250 asks $4,250, year unknown.
- A 2012 with 134k miles at $2,350 on Facebook Marketplace is almost certainly bogus.
- A 2015 IS 250 Sport with 109k miles asks $18,995 on Facebook Marketplace, over budget.
- Milwaukee IS 250 range: $2,000-$25,998, with 25,582-285,628 miles and about 41 listed. The Madison IS 250 average is cited as $13,484.

CT 200h: nationwide average $12,480, from $5,200. Supply: 40 listed in Madison, 53 in Milwaukee, and 67 in Green Bay (Edmunds). No individual CT listing with a price surfaced.

GS: CarGurus shows 77 GS listings in Wisconsin at $4,298-$48,672, and 49 of the 77 have no reported accidents. GS 350 nationwide average is $19,927, from $4,780. No individual GS listing with a price surfaced.

ES 300h and HS 250h: no priced listings surfaced. Lexus of Brookfield has a 2013 ES 300h (Stk 27466B), price unknown.

Dealer fees seen: Lexus of Brookfield charges a $479 dealer service fee on top of the price, plus tax, title, and registration.

Deal patterns: the cheapest Lexus sedans are at independent lots (Golden Cars on N Stoughton Rd in Madison, Mad Motors, Ramsey Motors in Milwaukee) and on Craigslist and Facebook. Franchise Lexus stores (Bergstrom, Brookfield, Milwaukee) mostly list cars over $15k, apart from occasional high-mileage trade-ins. Cars.com says Arlington, WI (near Madison) had the most Lexus deals under $10k: 18 great deals out of 67 listings, starting at $5,999.

These are only the figures the search summaries showed. Chicago metro, as of 2026-09-30:
- RX 350 AWD (CarGurus, near Chicago): 214 listings, $5,343 to $52,998, average about $11,823. 168 of the 214 report no accidents or damage.
- 2012 RX 350 AWD page (CarGurus, near Chicago): average about $12,376.
- 2012 RX 350 (Cars.com, national): average $12,947, starting at $7,950. Cars.com shows 28 RX 350s under $15k in Chicago.
- RX 350 (TrueCar, Schaumburg): 279 listings, $3,080 to $62,698.
- Carsforsale: 2011 RX 350s in Illinois start at $5,999.
- ES 350 (Edmunds, Chicago): a 2013 averages $15,348 with about 105,506 miles.
- ES 350 (Carsforsale): 61 in Chicago starting at $6,599. A 2011 starts at $7,995 and a 2009 at $2,000. Illinois-wide, 66 listings start at $9,977.

Price points for RX 350 AWD listings (a mixture of dealer and unconfirmed sources):
- 2010, about 97k miles: $13,490 (Palatine)
- 2012 by VIN, about 135k miles: $13,995 (Skokie)
- 2012 by VIN (summary says 2009), about 190k miles: $9,850 (Chicago)
- 2011, 80,912 miles, clean title, no accidents: $14,995 at Premium Auto Sales Inc, Palatine (VIN 2T2BK1BA0BC093752; above the cap)
- 2011, 59,324 miles: $17,985 (VIN 2T2BK1BA1BC115161, stock L3568; above the cap)

Pattern: a 2010–2012 RX 350 AWD with about 80–100k miles is asking $13.5k–15k in the Chicago suburbs. Below $10k usually means 150k+ miles or an unverified listing. The Tinley Park 2013 RX at $9,990 is the only possible under-priced find, but its data conflicts and it must be verified.

Lexus of Arlington in Arlington Heights has a dedicated 'Vehicles Under $15k' bargain page (lexusofarlington.com/bargain-inventory/index.htm), which is worth checking directly.

Wisconsin comparison: not possible. No Wisconsin searches were run before the search pool ran out, so there is no WI data to compare against.

Search-summary caveat: two summaries gave the wrong model year for a VIN, and one gave a price and features that cannot belong to a 2013 RX. Every price, mileage and VIN must be confirmed on the dealer page before it is used.

market_notes:
SUMMARY: I found 13 concrete listings. 11 come from Facebook Marketplace category pages around Chicago and fit the <= $13,500 cap; the other 2 are dealer listings on Capital One Auto Navigator, one with no price shown and one $499 over the cap. I found no qualifying Land Rover listing inside Madison or Dane County, and no individual listings for Evoque, Discovery Sport, LR2 or LR3 at all. The LR4 is the cheapest and most plentiful Land Rover under $13.5K.

1) OBSERVED ASKING-PRICE RANGES (from the search results only)
- LR4, Chicago: CarGurus shows 70 listings at $6,367-$39,734, and 43 of 70 have no reported accident. TrueCar shows $6,275-$36,000 with 32,628-180,496 miles (cargurus.com/Cars/l-Used-Land-Rover-LR4-Chicago-d2041_L7510; truecar.com .../lr4/location-chicago-il/).
- 2013 LR4:
  - Chicago average list price $13,889 at 108,517 average miles; Illinois range $7,990-$27,000 (edmunds.com/used-2013-land-rover-lr4-chicago-il/).
  - Nationwide average $10,606 (from $6,900) or $10,278.
  - KBB dealer range for a 2013 LR4 HSE is $7,875-$10,400. Edmunds appraisal value for a 2013 LR4 is $3,903-$8,348 (edmunds.com/land-rover/lr4/2013/appraisal-value/). This approximates the trade-in or private resale value.
- LR4 averages: Cars.com $13,601-$14,967. Edmunds shows 395 listings at $3,732-$20,990, average $13,475.
- LR4, Wisconsin:
  - Green Bay/Sheboygan average $15,076, range $8,397-$28,243.
  - Milwaukee Auto Navigator $13,999-$19,995.
  - Eau Claire: a 2014 LR4 HSE with 84,875 miles at $16,446 including dealer fees.
  - Janesville Autotrader: 2011/2015/2016 LR4s at $23,995-$30,988 (all over budget).
  - Hales Corners WI: a 2016 LR4 HSE with 99,150 miles, price not shown.
  - Rockford IL: an LR4 (listed as 2016 in one result and 2013 in another) with 96K miles at $13,995-$14,995.
  - Facebook: a 2016 LR4 in Downers Grove with 82K miles at $17,800.
- Range Rover Sport:
  - 2011 nationwide average $10,573 (from $5,000). 2012 average $12,269 (from $6,999). 2012 HSE average $9,759 (from $3,000).
  - Cars.com Chicago: a 2012 RRS HSE with 92,800 miles at $15,950.
  - Carfax shows 2012 RRS HSEs in Kenosha (12,637 miles) and Racine (41,129 miles). Prices not shown; low miles, likely over budget.
- Evoque:
  - Madison: 43+ listings at $6,995-$63,844 with 5-170,949 miles (TrueCar).
  - Waukesha: $9,950-$59,777.
  - Chicago: $8,343-$55,790. The 2015 Chicago average list is $19,798.
  - 2014 nationwide average $9,970 (from $6,900); 2013 from $6,995.
  - No individual Evoque at or under $13.5K surfaced in my searches.
- Discovery Sport: Chicago $6,388-$59,251. The Edmunds retail value (TMV) for a 2015 HSE with 96K miles is $16,322, so sub-$13K examples would be high-mileage or damaged.
- LR2: nationwide average $8,178 (from $4,000); 137 nationally from $4,495; 16 in West Bend WI.
- Wisconsin overall: 59 used Land Rovers from $6,399 (carsforsale.com).

Deal patterns:
- Sub-$13K Land Rovers in this region are almost all 110K-230K miles.
- Facebook Marketplace is where the lowest asks appear. Several are implausibly low ($2,800-$6,500 for 2011-2016 models) and should be treated as salvage, a known failure, a down-payment-only ad, or a scam until the VIN and title are checked.
- The only franchise Land Rover dealer found in Madison is Land Rover Madison / Fields JLR Volvo (504 E Badger Rd, Madison WI 53713, 608-443-3600). It retails newer certified pre-owned (CPO) stock and is not a source of sub-$13K cars.

2) COMMON EXPENSIVE FAILURES AND REPAIR COSTS
Not verified this run: the shared search budget ran out before I could search repair sources. Everything in this section is general background knowledge and every dollar figure is an ESTIMATE to confirm with RepairPal or an independent Land Rover specialist.
- LR3 and LR4 (2010-13, 5.0 V8), Range Rover Sport (2006-13), Range Rover L322 (2006-12):
  - Air suspension: compressor about $800-1,500; each air strut or spring about $500-1,500 installed; ride-height sensors and valve block also fail. Many owners convert to coil springs for about $1,000-2,000.
  - 5.0 V8 (2010-13): timing-chain guide and tensioner wear, about $3,000-6,000. Plastic coolant crossover pipes and water pump, about $1,000-2,500.
  - 4.2 supercharged / 4.4 V8 (2006-09): cooling-system and water-pump issues, rear differential about $2,000-4,000.
  - All of these: electronic parking brake (EPB) module about $1,000-1,500; transfer-case motor; suspension bushings and control arms about $1,000+; valve-cover and oil leaks.
- LR4 2014-16 (3.0 supercharged V6): front timing-cover and oil-cooler leaks about $2,000-4,000; water pump.
- Evoque 2012-17 and Discovery Sport 2015-18 (2.0T):
  - ZF 9-speed shift quality and software problems (2014+).
  - Coolant and turbo issues.
  - Ingenium engine (2017+ Discovery Sport): timing-chain stretch.
  - Frequent electrical and infotainment faults.
- LR2 2008-12 (3.2 I6): transfer-case (PTU) and rear Haldex/differential failures about $1,500-3,000; electrical faults.
- An independent Land Rover shop typically charges about $130-180/hr (estimate). Madison has few LR specialists.

3) HOW DEALERS AND INSTANT-OFFER BUYERS TREAT 10+ YEAR-OLD LAND ROVERS
Only lightly sourced.
- Observed: CarMax Evoque search pages showed only newer units at $23,998-$30,998, including $25,998 at Schaumburg. No 10+ year-old Land Rovers appeared in CarMax retail results.
- Observed: the Edmunds appraisal value for a 2013 LR4 is $3,903-$8,348, against dealer asks of $7,875-$13,889. That gap is roughly $4K-6K between wholesale and retail.
- ESTIMATE / general knowledge: CarMax typically wholesales old, high-mileage luxury trade-ins through its auctions rather than retailing them. Carvana instant offers on 10+ year-old Land Rovers tend to be low or may be declined. Franchise dealers usually send them to auction. An Aug 2027 exit would therefore most likely be a private sale into a thin buyer pool, or a low wholesale-level trade-in.

4) IS A LAND ROVER UNDER $13K SENSIBLE FOR A 10-MONTH, ~9,000-MILE HOLD vs LEXUS GX OR RX?
All figures in this section are estimates.
- Fuel: an LR4 or RRS 5.0 V8 is rated 12-13 city / 17-18 highway, about 15 mpg combined. 9,000 miles is about 600 gallons, roughly $1,800-2,100. An RX350 at about 20 mpg uses about 450 gallons, roughly $1,400-1,600. A GX470 or GX460 is about 15-16 mpg, similar to the LR4.
- Depreciation: a $9-11K LR4 might lose roughly $1,500-3,000 over 10 months on paper. That is similar to a Lexus in dollars, but the Land Rover exit is much less certain: a thin private-buyer pool and wholesale-level trade-in bids.
- Repair risk: a single air-suspension, timing-chain or coolant-pipe event costs about $1,500-6,000 and would erase any purchase discount. Expected repair spend for a 110K-170K-mile LR4 or RRS over 10 months could plausibly be $1,500-4,000+, versus roughly $300-1,000 for a well-kept GX470 or RX350.
- Insurance: likely higher for a Land Rover than an RX, especially for a driver with little US history.
- Bottom line (estimate): a sub-$13K Land Rover is generally NOT the lowest-total-cost choice for a 10-month hold. The only exception is an LR4 bought well under market (about $9K or less) with a clean title, a documented recent air-suspension or cooling-system refresh, and a clean PPI from a Land Rover specialist. Even then, a Lexus GX470 or RX350 is the safer lowest-total-cost pick because of its much lower repair variance and easier resale. If a Land Rover is chosen, the 2015 Naperville LR4 HSE Lux ($11,490, 124K miles) and the 2016 Lake Bluff LR4 ($11,999, 133K miles) are the most reasonable-looking listings found. The 2013 Summit Argo LR4 ($8,985, 129K miles) is the cheapest one that does not look implausible.

market_notes:
These are aggregate figures from search summaries, all for the Chicago area, seen 2026-09-30.
CAMRY:
- 2014 Camry: about 98 listed. Average price $12,036-$12,180. Average mileage about 129,700.
- 2015 Camry: about 116 listed. Average price $12,041-$12,675. Average mileage about 127,800. On Carsforsale, the cheapest of 10 Chicago listings was $11,899 with 128k miles.
- Camry SE (all years): 140 listed at $5,703-$27,998, average about $8,309. 111 of the 140 have no reported accidents.
- Takeaway: a 2014-2015 Camry near $12k usually has about 125-130k miles. One with under 100k miles (e.g. the 2014 LE with 78k miles, Good Deal, Arlington Heights; the 2015 LE with 95.6k miles, CARS R US Chicago) would be the better buy for resale, if the price stays at or below $13.5k.
RAV4:
- 2013 RAV4: 106 listed at $3,900-$21,998, average about $11,935. 65 of the 106 have no reported accidents.
- Averages for AWD LE: 2014 about $14,502; 2015 about $14,694. Both are above the $13.5k cap.
- RAV4 LE AWD (all years): 225 listed from $9,910. RAV4 XLE AWD (all years): 198 listed from $9,372.
- AWD 2013-2015 RAV4s under $12.5k near Chicago almost always have 140-190k miles. Examples: $11,398 / 139.7k; $11,991 / 155k (1-owner, $1,335 below CARFAX Value); $12,499 / 143.5k.
- Takeaway: a low-mileage AWD RAV4 under $13.5k is scarce. The Camry offers better value per mile in this budget.
CARFAX filters for Chicago RAV4s: 156 1-owner, 180 AWD.
Caution: the search summaries sometimes mixed up data across listings. One VIN showed two conflicting price/mileage records, and a second VIN, 2T3RFREV1EW191736, returned inconsistent data and was dropped. Verify every listing with the dealer before acting.
search_coverage:
